Cafe An: A Tranquil Escape in the Heart of Hanoi
Feb 2024 • Friends
This is one of my favorite coffee shops when I come to Vietnam. Cafe An is a charming and peaceful cafe located in a quiet area of Hanoi. The cafe’s interior blends modern design with traditional Vietnamese elements, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere. It’s a perfect place to unwind, read, or enjoy a cup of coffee. The menu offers a variety of drinks, with a highlight on Vietnamese iced coffee, which is rich and refreshing. The staff is friendly and attentive, providing excellent service. Located near the Old Quarter, it’s an ideal spot to relax after exploring the city. Whether you’re a coffee lover or simply seeking a calm place, Café An is a must-visit in Hanoi.

Discrimination
Dec 2024 • Solo
I had an unsettling experience at the shop today that I feel compelled to share. As a Vietnamese Canadian visiting my hometown, I was shocked to encounter a clear sense of discrimination during my visit.

It seemed like the shop primarily catered to foreign tourists. Despite being a resident and returning to my roots, I felt like an outsider in a place that should embrace all patrons equally.

The staff appeared disinterested and dismissive towards local people.

I truly hope that An Bread can recognize the importance of treating all customers with respect and inclusivity. Discrimination has no place in our communities, especially in such a beloved gathering spot. Until this issue is addressed, I cannot recommend this coffee shop to others. There are many fantastic local spots that welcome everyone with open arms.

Experienced racism in my own country
Oct 2024 • Solo
I experienced racism in my own country. Vietnamese cannot sit in front of this shop, if they know you are Vietnamese, they will said this table has been reserved and then they make you sit in the aisle. No wifi, just cash only, waited nearly 1 hour to be served drinks. They deliberately cleaned up the tables and chairs next to me, to show their impoliteness and indignation? Even street vendors accept bank transfers, but the owner of this shop only accepts cash.
They treat foreign guests very thoughtfully and warmly, so they receive many good reviews from foreign tourists. But on the contrary, they treat Vietnamese people very impolitely and unfriendly. 
As a Vietnamese person, I am very sad because of their way of doing this. Because of their own xenophilia, they have ruin the inherent friendly and hospitable image of Vietnamese people

The best spot to watch the world go by! Exceptional food, drinks, service and atmosphere.
Oct 2024 • Couples
Cannot recommend this little spot highly enough. The food, drinks and atmosphere are amazing! We ordered coffees and Bahn mi and then ordered more off the menu (smoothie) as the coffees were so good. Smoothie was equally as good!! The staff are wonderful, attentive and friendly. Ordered an egg coffee and they literally drew me in the coffee!! Sunglasses and all! What a cute little cafe. Wish we were in Hanoi longer so we could come again! The best little spot to watch the world go by.
